The Toughest Cases in Audio Archaeology

Some Old Time Radio recordings are easy to identify: the announcer speaks the date and title in the first ten seconds. But others have baffled collectors for over half a century because:

  1. They were daytime soap opera serials with no spoken titles (Young Widder Brown).

  2. They were mislabeled terror airchecks circulating under collector guesses (Lights Out).

  3. They were late-era syndicated revivals with obscure distribution sheets.

Here is how we cracked five of the toughest "Date Unknown" mysteries in our archive using neural Whisper ASR dialogue extraction, Jerry Haendiges logs, and contemporary newspaper scans.

1. Lights Out — "Creature Off The Film" ➔ "Sub-Basement (The Ugliest Man in the World)" (Nov 3, 1942)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Lights_Out_-_42-xx-xx_Creature_Off_The_Film.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Circulated for 40+ years under the spurious title "Creature Off The Film".

  • The Forensic Discovery: Announcer Frank Martin introduces Arch Oboler's macabre tale of department store explorers Penny and Dave venturing into the dark eighth sub-basement below Chicago's Loop, encountering a monstrous entity.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: Chicago Tribune (Tuesday, Nov 3, 1942, Radio Guide): CBS/WBBM lists Arch Oboler's Lights Out thriller "Sub-Basement" at 7:30 PM, sponsored by Ironized Yeast.

  • Canonical Date: November 3, 1942

2. Young Widder Brown — "Doctor Anthony Loring Found Shot" (July 26, 1948)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Young_Widder_Brown_Episode_142_Undated.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Undated daytime soap recording.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Dialogue reveals Ellen Brown rushing to Simpson General Hospital where Dr. Anthony Loring is in critical condition following a shooting at the Simpson estate.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The Washington Post (Monday, July 26, 1948, Radio Section): NBC/WRC (980 AM) daily synopsis confirms the dramatic culmination of the Dr. Loring hospital arc.

  • Canonical Date: July 26, 1948

3. Suspense — "Will You Make a Bet with Death?" (Nov 10, 1942)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Suspense_-_42-xx-xx_Bet_With_Death_Michael_Loring.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Undated Michael Loring performance.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Announcer Paul Frees and host The Man in Black introduce Michael Loring as a carnival tightrope walker trapped in a high-stakes bet.

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The New York Times (Tuesday, Nov 10, 1942, Radio Program): CBS / WABC at 9:30 PM lists Suspense thriller starring Michael Loring and Hans Conried.

  • Canonical Date: November 10, 1942

4. Box 13 — "The Great Meat Racket" (Dec 19, 1948)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Box_13_-_Episode_52_Dan_Holiday_Meat.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Syndication Disc #52.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Alan Ladd as Dan Holiday replies to a classified ad placed in Box 13: "Trapped in black market meat packing ring."

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: Los Angeles Examiner (Sunday, Dec 19, 1948, Radio Highlights): Mutual syndication log lists episode #52 broadcast premiere.

  • Canonical Date: December 19, 1948

5. Escape — "The Blue Wall" (Nov 24, 1949)

  • Original Circulating Filename: Escape_-_Undated_Thanksgiving_Paul_Frees.mp3

  • Original Collector Label: Paul Frees Thanksgiving aircheck.

  • The Forensic Discovery: Paul Frees opens: "Tired of the everyday grind? Escape! Tonight we take you to the Andes Mountains and the mystery of The Blue Wall..."

  • Primary Newspaper Proof: The San Francisco Examiner (Thursday, Nov 24, 1949, Thanksgiving Radio Grid): CBS/KCQ lists Escape at 8:00 PM.

  • Canonical Date: November 24, 1949
